subject: Aligning renewal uplift with consumption triggers — credit recapture discussion
messages:
From: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@acme.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal uplift — consumption thresholds and credit recapture

Jonas / Ben,

We're working through our renewal and wanted to bring up an issue that came up internally around how uplift interacts with actual consumption. The short version: our usage for Q3 exceeded our committed tier by ~35% (report attached), and procurement expects a predictable approach to credits/true-ups tied to consumption.

A few asks from our side:
- Can you outline a mechanism where we only trigger a credit recapture when usage sustains above a threshold for two consecutive months (we're thinking 120% of committed)?
- Can you provide a softened recapture option if usage spikes are short-lived (e.g., temporary burst protection for 1 month)?
- We need clarity on how any legacy discount we'd had will be handled if we accept an uplift. Can some discount be preserved for a transition period?

Attached: Q3_Usage_Report.csv

We'd like to lock terms this week if possible. Procurement contact is procurement@acme.com. Happy to hop on a quick call if that's easier.

Thanks,
Sara Lewis
Head of Platform Integrations
Acme, Inc.
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal uplift — consumption thresholds and credit recapture

Sara — thanks for the data and the clear asks. We can propose two pragmatic paths that balance predictability for Acme and risk management for Redwood: 

Option A — Laddered true-up (recommended)
- 0-119% of committed: no recapture.
- 120-149%: trigger a laddered credit recapture at 50% of uplift differential (measured monthly, applied at next invoice).
- 150%+: full recapture (100%) of uplift delta for months over threshold.
- Sustained requirement: credit recapture only applies if threshold is exceeded in 2 consecutive months (your ask).

Option B — Burst buffer + quarterly true-up
- Provide a 1-month burst buffer up to +35% without any recapture (protects short spikes).
- Quarterly true-up applies after that; reconciled and capped at a maximum effective recapture percentage to limit one-off shocks.

On legacy discount: we can grandfather a portion of the previous discount for a single billing quarter while the uplift ladder phases in — e.g., 50% of legacy discount preserved for 90 days post-amendment. After that, new pricing applies.

I'll loop in Monica on the invoicing implications and Ben will send a short pricing matrix with example invoices. If this direction sounds reasonable, I'll draft an amendment language we can share with procurement.

Proposed next step: 30-minute call today 3:00–3:30pm PT.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@acme.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal uplift — consumption thresholds and credit recapture

Sara / team — attaching a worked example so you can see the math. Key points from the pricing side: 

- We modeled committed tier = 1.0M tokens/month. Q3 actual average = 1.35M.
- Under Option A laddering, the sample month shows a 50% recapture on the 120–149% band which reduces single-month invoice volatility.
- We cap total annual recapture at 1.5x committed over the year to avoid runaway billing.
- Legacy discount handling: we can stage it down over one quarter (50% preserved) or accelerate to immediate removal if Acme prefers a cleaner monthly rate.

See attached: proposed_pricing_matrix.xlsx (pricing band examples + sample invoices).

Two asks from our side before we finalize language:
1) Confirm PO process and whether we need the amendment to include specific invoicing addresses (procurement@acme.com?).
2) Confirm whether Acme requires the contract to reference specific usage artifacts (e.g., S3 usage logs / our token meter) for auditability.

Happy to jump on the call at 3pm PT.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Lead Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@acme.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2026-09-20T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal uplift — consumption thresholds and credit recapture

Ben / Jonas — thanks, that matrix is helpful. A couple of comments from procurement: 

- Procurement wants the 1-month burst buffer but asks that the laddering start at 130% instead of 120% to reduce admin churn. Are you able to move that threshold?
- For legacy discount: we'd like to keep 25% of the current discount for one quarter (not 50%) — that's our internal mandate for existing customers undergoing pricing changes.
- Procurement also needs a short clause on invoice proration and PO timing; attaching our PO instructions.

Attached: PO_instructions.pdf

If you can accommodate the 130% ladder start and the 25% one-quarter legacy discount, we can proceed to an amendment. Call still works for 3pm.

—Sara
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@acme.com>
Date: 2026-09-21T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal uplift — consumption thresholds and credit recapture

Jonas / Ben / Sara — internal finance perspective and recommended compromise below.

Recommendation (compromise) — accept with guardrails:
1) Start ladder at 130% (as Acme requests). Apply laddered recapture at 50% for 130–149%, 100% for 150%+.
2) Preserve 25% of legacy discount for the first billing quarter following amendment (per procurement ask).
3) Include a 90-day review clause: after 90 days we reconvene and either formalize uplift or revert to standard pricing based on trailing 90-day consumption.
4) Add a cap to annual recapture to 1.5x committed to limit downside.

Contract language notes (draft pointers):
- "Consumption-triggered true-up" defined as: monthly meter > threshold in two consecutive months triggers reconciliation in the following invoice cycle.
- "Burst protection": first single-month overage up to 35% waived once per 12-month period.

I've created a HubSpot note with the recommended amendment text and linked the draft: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345 (see Deal: DL-ACME-2026-09).

If everyone is aligned I'll have Jon (legal ops) and I prepare an amendment draft for procurement and include the PO instructions you attached.

—Monica Patel
Director, Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-21T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Final: Amendment path & next steps — DL-ACME-2026-09

Thanks everyone — summary and next steps below.

Summary of agreed commercial terms (per Monica's recommendation):
- Laddered true-up starting at 130% sustained for 2 consecutive months. 130–149% -> 50% recapture; 150%+ -> 100% recapture.
- One-time 1-month burst buffer up to +35% with no recapture.
- Preserve 25% of legacy discount for one billing quarter post-amendment.
- Annual recapture cap = 1.5x committed.
- 90-day review clause to reassess uplift formalization.

Action items:
1) Jonas to send amendment draft to procurement@acme.com by EOD (attached).
2) Procurement to confirm PO details and signing authority.
3) Ben / Monica to prepare sample invoice schedule for first two quarters.

Attachments: amendment-draft_ACME_v1.docx

If that looks right, please confirm and I'll route to DocuSign once procurement confirms PO details.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — talk soon.

—Jonas
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com
